basis: Melanoma and neural-system tumors, typically astrocytomas, define this hereditary tumor syndrome.
Vertebral artery occlusion causes a posterior-circulation ischemic neurologic syndrome; arterial disease and cerebral ischemia define it.
Absent functional T lymphocytes define this combined immunodeficiency. Respiratory and intestinal infections do not establish intrinsic organ damage.
Myopia-associated degeneration of the retinal macula.
Primary endometrial carcinoma affects a reproductive organ outside the 13 axes.
Constriction of intracranial arteries defines the disease; hypoxic brain injury is a potential consequence rather than an obligatory manifestation.
Erythropoietic porphyrin-metabolism disorder with phototoxic skin damage; associated myeloid malignancy is a separately diagnosed disease.
Thyrotoxicosis, hypokalemia and skeletal-muscle paralysis define the condition. Arrhythmias occur in <30%; paralysis does not imply nerve damage.
Spastic paraplegia and polyneuropathy define it; acropathy/digital loss and knee or Achilles structural abnormalities accompany it, annotated at 30-79%.
Stage 5 chronic kidney failure; associated anemia, mineral-bone disease and cardiovascular diseases are separately diagnosed conditions.
A cavernous vascular neoplasm arising in and occupying the colon; both vascular origin and colonic site define it.
Colitis 80-99%; CNS infection and pneumonitis 30-79%. Retinitis/uveitis and hepatitis, each 30-79%, omitted under the four-axis cap.
Neuronal/glial degeneration defines NIID; scoliosis and structural vertebral abnormalities are annotated at 30-79%. Miosis and incontinence reflect neurologic dysfunction.
SPATA7-related inherited retinal degeneration.
Inherited coagulation-factor disorder with abnormal bleeding, prolonged bleeding time and reduced prothrombin consumption.
Autoimmune retinal injury mediated by antibodies against retinal proteins; the associated extraocular malignancy is a separate disease.
Malignant neoplasm arising in the external ear; no additional tissue involvement is established across this umbrella concept.
Inherited red-cell membrane disorder causing hemolysis. Hepatic manifestations are annotated at 5-29%; pseudohyperkalemia is not systemic electrolyte disease.
Generalized thyroid-hormone resistance defines endocrine dysfunction. Hearing loss and epiphyseal stippling lack frequency evidence sufficient for additional axes.
PRPH2-associated patterned dystrophy of the macula and retinal pigment epithelium.
Benign breast fibroadenoma; breast lies outside the 13 axes.
Axonal peripheral neuropathy; muscle fatty replacement, distal amyotrophy and pes cavus each reported in 2/2 patients, Achilles contracture in 1/1.
Sphingolipid-related axonal neuropathy; muscle atrophy 1/1 supports typical motor denervation. Ulcers/infections are secondary; cataract 1/1 does not establish typical eye involvement.
Fatty-acid oxidation defect; most individuals are asymptomatic. High neurologic/myopathy frequencies in small symptomatic cohorts do not establish ≥30% overall involvement.
Cerebellar/brain malformation and developmental impairment define it; polydactyly occurs in 50-75%; hypertrophic cardiomyopathy reported in 1/2, with limited sample size.
